questions.question: _____ unemployment happens when people are not able to find jobs during some months of the year.
questions.solution:
Sometime unemployment increase in a particular time of the year when the labour demand is lower than usual , this is called Seasonal unemployment.

For example

i. During festive season labour requirement is increased in every company, after festival labour requirement get decreased and seasonal unemployment happens.

ii. In case of tourism service higher employee is required only during the few months of the year, rest of the time seasonal unemployement happens.

questions.question: Which among the following comes under secondary sector of Indian Economy?
questions.solution:
There are basicaly three sector in Indian ecomony-

i. Primary Sector – This is basically take out things which are already provided by nature. It is also known as raw material production or delivery industry. Ex- Crop production, cotton production, transport of goods.

ii. Secondery sector – In this sector human activity transform raw material into products or goods. It is basically production industry.Ex- Textile andCloth industry, food manufacturing.

iii. Tertiary Sector – It is service sector that gives value to people but not physical goods. Ex – Banking, Army or Police service etc.

So, Cloth industry which produce cloths from cotton or others raw materials, comes under secondery sector of Indian economics.

questions.question: In which economic system the goods produced are distributed among people not on the basis of what people need but on the basis of Purchasing Power?
questions.solution: Capitalism is an economy system in which the means of production are privately owned and operated for profit, usually in cometitive markets. In system the goods produced are distributed among people not on the basis of what people need but on the basis of Purchasing Power.

questions.question: Which among the following is an example of progressive tax?
questions.solution:
A progressive tax is a tax in which the tax rate increases as the taxable amount increases. That means low tax imposed on low income earners compared to those with a higher income.

Excise duties, Octroi, House tax all are fixed but income tax is different for different earning people.

questions.question: In which year 'New Economic Policy' was announced in India?
questions.solution:
Beginning with mid-1991, the govt. has made some radical changes in economic policies bearing on trade, foreign investment exchange rate, industry, fiscal discipline etc. The new economy system introduces to improve the productivity and efficiency of the system. Main three parts of new economy system are –

Liberalisation: In this policy private sector has been freed from licensing and other restrictions.

Privatisation: Privatisation means permitting the private sector to set up industries which were previously reserved for the public sector. Under this policy many PSU’s were sold to private sector. 

Globalization: Globalisation means the interaction of the domestic economy with the rest of the world with regard to foreign investment, trade, production and financial matters.

questions.question: Who among the following is a part of political executive?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option (3) i.e. Finance Minister

 
• There are three pillars of the democracy namely Legislature, Executive, Judiciary.
 
• The role of **Legislature is to Make and enact the law.**
 
• The role of the **executive is to execute and enforce the Law.**
 
• The role of **Judiciary is to interpret and apply the law.**
 
• There is** no watertight separation between Legislature and Executive.**
 
• Those executives which are** drawn from the Legislature are known as the Political Executive** because they are elected by the people.
 
• **Finance Minister is the Political Executive**.

questions.question: Which among the following country is a ‘Third World Country'?
questions.solution:
After World War II the world split into two large geopolitical blocs and spheres of influence with contrary views on government and the politically correct society: 

1 - First World: refers to so called developed, capitalist, industrial countries, roughly, a bloc of countries aligned with the United States after World War II. Ex – North America, Japan, Australia.

2 - Second World: It refers to the former communist-socialist, industrial states. Ex: Russia, Poland. China.

3 - Third World: All the other countries, today often used to roughly describe the developing countries of Africa, Asia and Latin America.

questions.question: How many Mahajanpadas were there in ancient India?
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is __16__.

 
• During the lifetime of Lord Gautam Buddha,** sixteen Mahajanpadas** existed in the 7th and early 6th centuries BC.
 
• Mahajanpadas were the major kingdoms of Vedic India during the 6th Century BC.

 
• Kasi: Varanasi 
 
• Kosala: Ayodhya
 
• Anga: Champa 
 
• Magadha: For a time, Rajgir (known as Rajagriha in the past) was the capital, which was then shifted to Pataliputra 
 
• Vajji: Vaishali
 
• Malla: Kushinara and Pava
 
• Chedi: Sothivati (Near Banda in Uttar Pradesh)
 
• Vatsa or Vamsa: Kaushambi (Near Modern Allahabad)
 
• Kuru: Indraprastha 
 
• Panchala: Ahichatra (Northern Panchala) and Kampilya (Southern Panchala)
 
• Matsya: Viratanagari 
 
• Surasena: Mathura
 
• Assaka: Potana or Potali 
 
• Avanti: Ujjain
 
• Gandhara: Taxila
 
• Kamboj: Rajapura

 
• Buddha was born in **563 BC.**
 
• Buddha was born at Lumbini, near Kapilavastu in Nepal.

questions.question: Which of the following cell organelles is present only in plant cell?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cell Wall**__.

__
 
• A cell wall is a rigid layer of polysaccharides lying outside the plasma membrane of the cells of plants, fungi, and bacteria.
 
• In the algae and higher plants, it consists mainly of cellulose.

Plant cell wall:

 
• The plant cell wall is made up of cellulose and pectin__.
 
• It provides a structural framework to support the growth of plants.
 
• The cell wall also acts as the first line of defence against pathogens.

__
 
• A plant cell consists of a cell wall__ for structural rigidity and tough environmental conditions. The cell wall consists of three layers. 

 
 
• The primary cell wall
 
• secondary cell wall
 
• middle lamella.
 
 
 
• The primary wall is composed of up to 50% Hemicellulose, cellulose 25%, and other smaller amounts of pectic substances, non-polysaccharides, fats, and proteins. The primary wall is the cellulose-containing layer laid down by cells that are dividing and growing.
 
• The secondary wall is composed of Lignin. Secondary cell walls provide additional protection to cells and rigidity and strength to the larger plant. Lignin makes the wall thick and rigid.
 
• Middle lamella is composed of Pectin. The middle lamella serves as a cementing layer between the primary walls of adjacent cells. The two cells can be separated from each other by the dissolution of the middle lamella by proteolytic enzymes.

questions.question:
Which among the following is/are output devices?

I. Scanner

II. Speaker

III. Plotter
questions.solution:
An input device is any hardware device that sends data to a computer, allowing you to interact with and control it.

An output device is any hardware that sends data from a computer to another device mostly in form of audio or video.

 
• Scanner scans any document and sends it to computer, so it is a input device.
 
• Speaker gets data from computer in form of audio. So it is a output device.
 
• Plotter is printer that print vector image. It recieve data from computer and print it on paper. So it is also a output device.

questions.question: Under MUDRA Bank, loan ranging from Rs. 50,000 to Rs. 5,00,000 is categorized under _____.
questions.solution:

The interventions have been named ‘Shishu’, ‘Kishor’ and ‘Tarun’ to signify the stage of growth / development and funding needs of the beneficiary micro unit.

1. Shishu: covering loans up to Rs. 50,000

2. Kishor: covering loans above Rs. 50,000 and up to Rs. 5 lakh
